CIV.note: Risks such as fake videos and bias are only discussed by a speaker; no rule or authority stated.

facts.fact: KOACI reports that at the National Assembly session of 12 October 2026 the conversational assistant Aya was demonstrated to Assembly president Patrick Achi, who tried it on budget analysis and legislative information search.

CIV.note: Education, health and agriculture AI uses were described by a Moroccan guest as possibilities; nothing stated for Cote d'Ivoire.

facts.fact: KOACI reports a WhatsApp assistant answering written or voice messages in Baoule and Malinke, presented by Dr Isaac Bayoh on 12 October 2026 as the result of over two years of research and a base of over 50,000 validated sentences and about 17,000 hours of speech.

Minister Djibril Ouattara said the 2026-2028 digital roadmap provides for training more than 2,000 public officials in AI by the end of 2027, and an AI awareness and training session for deputies was held at the National Assembly on 12 October 2026.

CIV.note: Training named is for deputies and public officials, not the public.
Only a general statement that data feeding AI should be controlled by Cote d'Ivoire; no plan or rule on state data.

facts.fact: Minister Djibril Ouattara presented the 2026-2028 digital roadmap, aligned with the 2026-2030 national development plan, with 440 structuring projects on six pillars, at the National Assembly on 12 October 2026; no adoption is stated.
KOACI gives the digital roadmap's period as 2026-2028.
